text:
Priya: On a customer call, they tried the Console -> Analytics -> Export CSV (Last 90 days, all filters) and downloaded a 0-byte file twice. They said sometimes it comes back as a .zip with a truncated CSV and weird characters for emojis and non-ascii names.

Ben: Thanks, Priya. Do we have a repro? Which org and dataset?

Priya: org: acme-inc (customer ticket #4567). Dataset: billing-events. Steps I followed: open analytics, set date range, click Export -> CSV (zipped). Downloaded file named export_2026-03-10.zip -> unzip -> 0 bytes.

Priya: I pulled the browser devtools network entry — response headers show: `content-type: application/octet-stream` and `content-disposition: attachment; filename="export_2026-03-10.zip"`. Response size header is `content-length: 0`.

Maya: Hmm. That suggests the server returned an empty body. Could be a streaming worker error or a failed s3 multipart put. Any server-side error id in the UI or logs?

Priya: Support logs show a 500 from export-service around the time: `export-service/1.3.2 ERROR 2026-03-10T18:12:03Z export_handler.go:145 failed to assemble archive: unexpected eof while reading`. I attached the partial stacktrace in the ticket.

Ben: Repro on my end in prod console? I tried exporting the same dataset for a truncated range and got a small zip with CSV but rows cut off mid-line, and some accented names became mojibake (Ã©).

Maya: The mojibake implies an encoding mismatch. We should ensure we set `Content-Encoding`/`charset` correctly when generating CSV. But the unexpected EOF hints at a streaming pipeline crash.

Jules: I'm checking S3: there are multipart uploads for that org at the same time, several completed, but one object (export-2026-03-10-176941-... .zip) is 0 bytes. The multipart complete call returned 200 but ETag looks odd. Upload logs show `ErrInvalidPart` during finalize for a subset.

Maya: OK assign to eng-runtime. @Maya can you add a canary to force a retry on failed multipart completes? Also we need better retries for multipart finalize.

Maya: Quick patch suggestion: catch io.ErrUnexpectedEOF in streaming concat and trigger abort+retry of multipart upload. I'll open a PR with a unit test that simulates a mid-stream connection drop.

Ben: For customer-facing workaround, ask them to export by splitting the date range into 30-day chunks — appears to avoid the multipart path and returns proper CSVs. Can we add that to the ticket?

Priya: Noted, I messaged the customer with the workaround. They also reported the file name encoding looked fine in Chrome but garbled in Excel on Windows. Might be Excel expecting UTF-16/LE BOM.

Maya: Good call. For CSV encoding we should emit UTF-8 with a BOM optional header when `client=excel` or add an `Export -> Encoding` dropdown in Console. Short-term: add `EFF` (UTF-8 BOM) at the start of CSVs for legacy Excel compatibility for exports > 1MB. I'll include this in the PR.

Ben: Also adding a monitoring alert: exports returning size=0 or Content-Length mismatch > 0.5% should create a Sev2.

Priya: Customer updated: they retried with 30-day chunks and got full files, but asked for ETA. Estimated fix ETA?

Maya: I'll aim for a hotfix today to add retry and BOM, then follow-up with a proper resilience refactor next sprint.

Ben: Thanks. I've linked the ticket (#4567) and created a follow-up incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/exports-2026-03-10 (internal).

ExportBot: Export job 1769412358 for org acme-inc terminated with status=failed, error=ErrInvalidPart (logged).

Priya: Perfect — leaving notes in the ticket and pinging customer after the hotfix. :thumbsup:
